notes: SEQN is the unique participant identifier in NHANES. It maps to person_source_value to link all records to the same individual.

Dietary day one sample weight is a survey design weight. It can be stored as an observation with a custom concept for the weight type, or used in analysis but not directly mapped to a standard clinical field.
Dietary two-day sample weight is a survey design weight. Similar to WTDRD1, stored as an observation value.
Food/Individual component number is an ordinal identifier for food items within a dietary recall. It can be stored as an observation value or in a custom dietary extension table.
Dietary recall status is a categorical variable indicating the quality/completeness of the recall. It maps to value_as_concept_id with a corresponding custom concept.
Interviewer ID code is an identifier for the interviewer. It can be stored as an observation string or in the provider table if interviewers are considered providers.
Breast-fed infant status. Concept 40767445 is 'Breastfeeding status' or a similar binary concept can be used. Alternatively, a custom concept for NHANES-specific variable.
Number of days of intake is a categorical variable. It can be mapped to a custom concept representing the number of dietary recall days.
Number of days between intake and household interview is a continuous variable. Stored as value_as_number with a custom observation concept.
Intake day of the week is categorical. Can be mapped to a custom concept for days of the week.
Language respondent used mostly. Can be mapped to a standard language concept if available, or a custom concept.
Combination food number is an ordinal identifier for combination foods. Stored as value_as_number.
Combination food type is a categorical/text description. Stored as value_as_string or mapped to a custom concept.
Time of eating occasion (HH:MM) is a time value. OMOP does not have a dedicated time field, so it can be stored as value_as_string or converted to a numeric representation.
Name of eating occasion (e.g., breakfast, lunch) is categorical. Can be mapped to a custom concept for meal types.

Source of food is a categorical variable describing where the food came from. It can be mapped to an Observation with a concept representing the source (e.g., store, restaurant). A specific standard concept_id is not provided here; it would need to be looked up in the vocabulary.
Binary variable indicating if the meal was eaten at home. Can be mapped to an Observation with standard concepts for Yes/No (e.g., 4188539 for Yes, 4188540 for No).

USDA food code is an identifier for the food item. It can be stored as a string in the observation table. Alternatively, it could be mapped to a standard concept if a food ontology is used, but typically it is a source code.
Grams of food consumed. This is a continuous measurement. The concept_id for 'Grams' or 'Mass' would need to be identified (e.g., LOINC code).
Energy in kcal. Standard concept for 'Energy' (kcal) is 4267696 (LOINC 55423-0).
Protein in grams. Standard concept for 'Protein intake' is 40762399 (SNOMED 226356005).
Carbohydrate in grams. Standard concept for 'Carbohydrate intake' is 40762400 (SNOMED 226358006).
Total sugars in grams. Standard concept for 'Sugars intake' is 3005770 (LOINC 55331-5).
Dietary fiber in grams. Standard concept for 'Fiber intake' is 3005771 (LOINC 55333-1).
Total fat in grams. Standard concept for 'Total fat intake' is 40762401 (SNOMED 226357001).
Total saturated fatty acids in grams. Standard concept for 'Saturated fat intake' is 3005769 (LOINC 55330-7).
Total monounsaturated fatty acids in grams. A standard concept for monounsaturated fat intake is not readily available in common OMOP vocabularies; may require a custom concept or LOINC code.
Total polyunsaturated fatty acids in grams. Similar to monounsaturated, a standard concept is not commonly defined; may need a custom concept.
Cholesterol in mg. Standard concept for 'Cholesterol intake' is 3005768 (LOINC 55329-9).
